title: Giving Way on Purpose: Cartesian Impedance for an Arm That Meets a Surface, Admittance for One That Cannot Be Torque Controlled, and Why Each Likes a Different Surface

artifact.note: making an arm behave as a spring and damper at its tool: Cartesian impedance (the joint torques that give the tool a wrench of stiffness times the pose error plus damping times the velocity error, through the transpose of the Jacobian, with the torque of gravity added), a surface that pushes back like a stiff spring with some damping, a run that presses the tool towards a point below the surface and reports the peak and settled force, and admittance (a virtual mass, damper and spring that turn the measured force into a displacement of the commanded position) for a tool that is position controlled, with a delay in the force and the inner loop's own lag
